tour.name: Rangiroa Private Day: the Blue Lagoon, the Pink Sands and the Dolphins of Tiputa Pass

tour.overview:
Rangiroa, in the Tuamotu archipelago, is one of the largest atolls in the world: a ring of coral islets around a lagoon some 80 kilometres long, so large that the island of Tahiti would fit inside. Its passes are famous among divers for sharks, manta rays and dolphins, and its remote Blue Lagoon, on the south-west side, is a shallow pool of brilliant turquoise enclosed by motus.

This private boat day takes you across the great lagoon to the Blue Lagoon with a local guide, with time for snorkelling, a picnic and, back near the villages, the dolphins of the Tiputa pass, a pearl farm and the atoll's unusual vineyard.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 8 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Rangiroa
• Type: private boat with captain and local guide
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy; the crossing can be bumpy

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Blue Lagoon.
• Pink sand beaches.
• A motu.
• The Tiputa pass.
• A pearl farm and the vineyard.

WHY THIS WORKS
A private boat lets you leave early for the long crossing and enjoy the Blue Lagoon before the day boats arrive.

WHO IT SUITS
Snorkellers, couples, families and nature lovers.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
Divers can add dives in the Tiputa pass with a dive centre.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Rangiroa is about 1 hour from Papeete by plane. The crossing to the Blue Lagoon takes about 1 hour and depends on the weather.

days.name: The Blue Lagoon, a motu picnic, the Tiputa pass dolphins, a pearl farm and the vineyard
days.description:
What to expect: the turquoise lagoons and the wildlife of a great atoll, by private boat.

Your boat leaves at about 8:00 and crosses the great lagoon, about an hour, to the Blue Lagoon. You wade and snorkel in the shallow turquoise water, where blacktip reef sharks patrol the sandy shallows and birds nest on the motus. You walk on beaches of pink sand, coloured by fragments of red coral, and have a picnic of grilled fish, poisson cru and coconut on a motu.

In the afternoon, you return to the Tiputa pass, where, as the tide flows, bottlenose dolphins often surf the waves at the entrance of the lagoon. You visit a pearl farm to see how the black-lipped oysters are grafted and the pearls harvested, and the vineyard of Rangiroa, where grapes grow on the coral sand of a motu, with a tasting of its white and rosé wines.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:00 – Departure by boat.
09:00 – Blue Lagoon and snorkelling.
11:00 – Pink sand beaches.
12:00 – Picnic on a motu.
14:00 – Return crossing.
15:00 – Tiputa pass dolphins.
15:45 – Pearl farm.
16:30 – Vineyard and tasting.
17:15 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The trip depends on the weather; the crossing can be cancelled in strong winds.
• Divers can see sharks, manta rays and dolphins in the pass.

INCLUDED: private boat and captain, local guide, snorkelling equipment, picnic, pearl farm, vineyard tasting, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: dives, alcoholic drinks with lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: How do we get to Rangiroa?
faq.answer: By Air Tahiti, about 1 hour from Papeete; we can book flights.

faq.question: What if the weather is bad?
faq.answer: If the crossing is unsafe, we replace it with a lagoon tour near the passes or another date.

faq.question: Are the sharks dangerous?
faq.answer: Blacktip reef sharks are shy and not dangerous if you follow your guide’s advice.

faq.question: Will we see dolphins?
faq.answer: Very often at the Tiputa pass, especially on the incoming tide; never guaranteed.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, a picnic on a motu.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Child life vests are provided.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly; boarding and landing on beaches need some agility.

faq.question: What should we bring?
faq.answer: Swimwear, a towel, a hat, sunglasses, reef-safe sun cream and a windproof layer for the crossing.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: All year. December to March is best for hammerhead sharks for divers.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is not customary in French Polynesia and is never expected, but a small gesture for excellent service is always appreciated.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 72 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
